main_body: A slot machine cabinet: a gold crown/header block at the top, then a red body with a reel window (white and red symbols with black dividers), a coin tray and a dark payout slot, on a brown base. All of it is drawn flat from the front.
top_band: Rows 1-4 are a gold band (L=173), but it is the machine's header panel seen face-on. It is not a horizontal surface. Rows 5-8 are dark brown below it, with no step marking a front edge. No top surface is visible.
evidence: The column at x=12 goes from a 1-row outline to a gold block (rows 1-4) and then straight into a long flat face (rows 5-26, 22 rows of the same L=72). The gold block reads as a sign or header panel, not a top, and it is 4 rows of front-facing decoration. The reel window, tray and slot are painted flat, with no inset edges and no eave shadow. The whole machine is a front elevation, so it fails the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has 12 distinct colours and a median of 12 per tile, against 38-40 distinct colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. Flat-fill coverage is 0%. Only 17% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines lean brown and read as dark material tone. Shading is limited to about 4 steps per material (gold, brown, red). Texture is limited to the symbol blocks and a few highlight pixels, with no grain on the large brown and red areas. The piece is clean but thinner than the Beodeul references, and it looks flatter next to them.
